readings: §5.9's own warning holds: the /^[a-z]+\.[a-z_]+$/ regex also matches filenames and any other dotted lowercase literal; every hit is quoted so the contract's documented ⊆ observed test can be read against its source
a type value that is a name or attribute is resolved against module-level string constants of this file or of a sibling module imported by it (ADAPTED — see the module docstring)
keys are sorted; open_keys records {**expansion} and updates records .update(...) on the bound name, both of which mean the key list is a lower bound for that shape

a site leaves shapes only on proof that it is not an event constructor (NARROWED — E1: the "type" value can never be a str, which chain.py:192 refuses; E2: every value in the dict is a constant-key read of one same other object, the "type" included, so the dict re-describes an event rather than naming one). Every dropped site is quoted in provenance.excluded

inability to prove a dict IS an event is NOT one of those tests. constructor_evidence records reaching chain.append when it can be shown, but a shape with no such evidence still stands: "we could not look" must not read as "there is nothing there"

shapes therefore stays deliberately over-inclusive. It still holds JSON Schema fragments whose "type" is a plain string (mcp_server.py's "object"/"string"/"array"/"integer"/"boolean") and MCP content blocks ("text"). Separating those from a real bare-word event type such as chain.py's OUTCOME = "outcome" would need the known-type vocabulary, and PLAN §6 requires a new event type to cost zero engine changes — a vocabulary filter would silently drop exactly the new type it is most important to see. Over-inclusion is auditable from the quoted text; a wrong exclusion is not

a "type" that is a parameter or a branch-assigned local stays {"unresolved"}. Provenance names the values the population supplies, because that is evidence the site is a constructor, but it is not a resolution: those sites have more than one value and §5.9's shape type is one string
